item.title: Inside Week 10 of CIAC football: Return tickets, ticking clocks and the unbeatens
item.description: Berlin's Chace Hrubiec (12) drops back for a pass during their game against Platt at Falcon Field in Meriden Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) It's almost that time. Playoff football is brewing, Thanksgiving is less than two weeks away, and numerous teams are on the edge of either clinching a spot in the tournaments or falling short of the postseason. An analysis of the field by GametimeCT had 11 teams unofficially clinching playoff berths heading into Week 10. That group featured some recent champions, such as Hand (2023 and 2025), Masuk (2024), Ansonia (2024), and Staples (2023). But there's plenty of room for newcomers. Of the 48 playoff spots, there are 20 teams that did not play in last year's tournaments that are inside the playoff bubble after Friday's games. Several of those teams have not appeared in the postseason in more than a decade, and one has never gone to the dance: Lewis Mills . Lewis Mills is in its 16th season as a program and now co-ops with Wolcott Tech , ranking sixth in Class L with a 6-2 record. Lyman Hall (M) and Plainville (SS) have both unofficially clinched berths in the playoffs. For Lyman Hall (7-2), it's the first bid since 2010, and for Plainville (9-0), it's the first since 2019. Pomperaug (8-1) is third in Class MM and is closing in on its first playoff berth since 2009, when it was runner-up in Class L. Xavier 's last trip to the playoffs resulted in a Class LL-Small championship in 2014. The Falcons (6-2) are seventh in Class MM. And one of the brightest stories in CIAC football this season, Simsbury , has gone from four wins in the last three years combined, to eight wins and a possible tournament berth. The Trojans are ranked fourth in Class L and should they qualify, it would be their first playoff appearance since 2019. The clock's ticking One of the many teams in need of a big win in Week 10 was defending Class M champion Berlin , which had taken a tough loss against Enfield in its most recent game. They got that bounce-back win by going back to the "old Berlin way." Berlin controlled the ball, the clock, and the game while rolling to a 26-0 win over Platt Thursday night in Meriden. Berlin had possession for 38 of 48 minutes and ran 51 plays to Platt's 20. "We had a horrible night versus Enfield. We didn't compete and we had to go to school the next day and it was a horrible feeling," Berlin coach John Capodice told GametimeCT's Bryant Carpenter. "We said, 'We've got to change this really, really quick. The clock's ticking. If you want to go into the playoffs and you want to be a quality football team, we had to go back to the old Berlin way, and that's competing for four quarters." By kicking it up a notch, Berlin improved to 6-3 and is in seventh place in the Class SS standings with one game remaining. It hosts Middletown (7-2) at 6:30 p.m., Friday. item.title: Aaron Wise Locks In New Titleist Driver For 2026 Season
item.description: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Aaron Wise has finalized his equipment setup for the late 2026 season, swapping in a new driver and wedge configuration. GolfWRX reported on November 14 that he is rolling with a Titleist GTS3 driver set at 10 degrees with a SureFit D1 setting. The shaft choice remains a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X, a staple for players seeking stability off the tee. This specific combination suggests a focus on consistency as the PGA Tour moves through its fall schedule. Wise keeps his 3-wood from TaylorMade, utilizing a Qi4D model at 15 degrees paired with a heavier Fujikura Ventus Black 8 TX shaft. The hybrid slot features a TaylorMade SIM2 Max at 19 degrees, loaded with a Project X HZRDUS Black 6.5 100G shaft. His iron set consists of Titleist T100 models from 4 through PW, all fitted with True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts. The wedges show the most significant change, with a Titleist Vokey Design SM11 52-12F bent to 51 degrees and a 56-08M adjusted to 55.5 degrees, alongside a Titleist Vokey Design WedgeWorks 60-L. All wedges carry True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts. Short Game and Putter Selection The putter remains a TaylorMade Corza Ghost, a design that offers a clean look for alignment. GolfWRX confirmed the grip choice across the bag is the Golf Pride Tour Velvet Cord, providing a secure hold in varying weather conditions. The ball selection stays with the Titleist Pro V1, a standard for players prioritizing spin control on approach shots. These details were posted on Saturday, November 14, reflecting the current state of Wise’s bag as he prepares for upcoming events. What the Changes Mean Wise adjusted his wedge lofts to improve trajectory control around the greens. Bending the 52-degree wedge down to 51 and the 56-degree to 55.5 allows for tighter gapping between the pitching wedge and the sand wedge. The retention of the SIM2 Max hybrid suggests he still values the forgiveness of that club head, even as driver technology evolves. Sticking with the T100 irons shows confidence in the blade-like feel of the set, which demands solid contact but offers superior workability. The Fujikura Ventus Black shaft in the driver continues to be a top choice for the tour. Its stiffness profile helps manage face rotation, which is critical for maintaining accuracy. Wise’s setup aligns with many competitors who favor a high-launch, low-spin driver ball flight. The use of the Corza Ghost putter provides a counterbalance feel that can smooth out the stroke for players with a slight arc. Every component in this bag serves a specific purpose for a player competing at the highest level. Upcoming Schedule Context With the equipment list confirmed, Wise heads into the final stretch of the fall series. The focus now shifts to how these clubs perform under tournament pressure and varying course conditions. GolfWRX noted that more photos of the setup are available for fans to review.

item.title: Khamzat Chimaev blanks Chris Weidman with tech fall victory in RAF Abu Dhabi main event
item.description: Khamzat Chimaev put on another dominant performance to blank UFC Hall of Famer Chris Weidman in the RAF Abu Dhabi main event. Originally scheduled to face Colby Covington on Saturday, Chimaev accepted Weidman as a late notice replacement and showed why he’s such a danger on the wrestling mats. Chimaev poured on the offense and ultimately won off a challenge being denied after he used a four-point score that Weidman’s team didn’t agree with. The challenge was shut down and that gave Chimaev the clinching point to go up 10-0 and end the match by technical fall. “it feels good, it feels amazing,” Chimaev said about his win. “Anyone who wants to wrestle or fight, grapple, it doesn’t matter. I’m always ready.” Chimaev started strong and went up 5-0 in the first period after a takedown and turns on Weidman. To his credit, Weidman made Chimaev work for every position as he stayed in the match going into the second period. Weidman tried a slick move on the restart as he went for a slide by but Chimaev reversed positions for a four point score. That led to Weidman issuing challenge but that was denied giving Chimaev another point for the 10-0 technical fall victory. Chimaev has been unstoppable since arriving in RAF and it’s tough to believe the promotion won’t work tirelessly to rebook that match against Covington once he’s healthy enough to compete again.

item.title: Joseph scores record-equalling five tries as England rout Japan
item.description: Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell are the other players to have scored five tries in a single match for England [Getty Images] Nations Championship England (49) 78 Tries: Joseph 5, Steward, Genge, Murley, Earl, Martin, B Curry, M Smith, Fisilau Cons: Ford 4, Slade Pen: Ford Japan (10) 15 Tries: Dearns, Helu Con: Saito Pen: Saito Will Joseph marked his comeback after four years out the Test game with a record-equalling five tries as England tore through Japan and set their sights on New Zealand next weekend. A teenage Joseph made his debut as a late replacement in a game against Australia four years ago. Since then he has endured his boyhood club London Irish going bust, an underwhelming spell at Harlequins and the loss of hearing in his left ear after an auto-immune reaction. But his superb early season form for Gloucester has thrust him back into the international picture and he took his opportunity superbly, showing work-rate and intelligence as well as raw top-end speed. Four other players - Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell - have scored five tries in a single match for England. Japan were vastly over-matched, unable to rev up the ball movement and quickfire rucks that have made them a threat to the game's major powers in the past. With the outcome clear as England raced out to a 32-3 lead inside 20 minutes, the focus sharpened on a number of individuals attempting to press their case alongside Joseph. Centre Max Ojomoh, making his first appearance since an excellent performance against Argentina 12 months ago, was smart and sharp in midfield. The Bath man burst into a pocket of space to help set up Joseph's second and his slick hands opened up a corridor of space for his team-mate's gleefully acrobatic fourth as Japan were buried beneath an avalanche of points. Henry Pollock, afforded only his second start in his eye-catching England career, carried gamely but didn't have the impact he has shown so often off the bench. Replacement Greg Fisilau's pair of wince-inducing hits and burrowing try added more intrigue to the back-row equation. And while George Ford sewed together England's backline neatly enough, his failure to convert more of England's early tries won't help his hopes of regaining the 10 shirt on a more permanent basis. Northampton scrum-half Archie McParland made his debut as a replacement, but a host of front-line names will return next Saturday as England attempt to take down an All Blacks side smarting from defeat by Wales. item.title: RAF Abu Dhabi Highlights! Khamzat Steamrolls Weidman With 10-0 Shutout
item.description: Khamzat Chimaev didn’t miss a beat earlier today (Sat., Nov. 14, 2026) at RAF Abu Dhabi LIVE on FOX Nation from inside Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, as “Borz” dominated fellow former UFC middleweight champion Chris Weidman on short notice in the main event. Chimaev was originally expected to face former UFC welterweight contender Colby Covington in the RAF Abu Dhabi headliner before “Chaos” withdrew due to an undisclosed injury . Some believe Covington pulled out because of his shocking submission loss to Raul Rosas Jr. earlier this month, but it doesn’t really matter. Real American Freestyle (RAF) matchmakers were still forced to scramble and find a replacement to match up against Chimaev, which they did in Weidman. While Weidman is one of the better wrestlers to ever compete in UFC’s 185-pound division he’s currently 42 years old and coming off a decision loss to the aforementioned Covington at RAF 9 this past May. To say the odds were stacked against Weidman on short notice would be an understatement. Very few were giving him the chance to compete with Chimaev, let alone actually walk away with a win. In the end, it was too big of an ask for Weidman to step up on a few days notice and take out Chimaev. Instead, Chimaev had his way with Weidman like most expected, scoring five points in the first period. “Borz” opened the second period up with a four-point throw, which Weidman challenged and lost. item.title: Marlins Hit Coach Swap Ignores Real Progress Made In 2026
item.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports The Miami Marlins made a strange call by letting go of hitting coach Pedro Guerrero. Team president Peter Bendix announced the decision after the season ended. The front office claims they need a “new voice in the hitting space,” per reports. This reasoning does not hold up when looking at the actual numbers from the field. Guerrero Built a Real Foundation Guerrero left behind a lineup that actually improved. In 2024, the team finished 27th in runs and home runs. By 2025, they jumped to 18th in runs and 23rd in home runs. The offense also climbed to sixth in on-base percentage last year. Young players like Otto Lopez had a breakout All-Star campaign under his watch. Lopez led the majors with 191 base hits in 2026. Xavier Edwards and Kyle Stowers also developed well during this time. The stats show a clear upward trend that took two years to build. Lawson Has a Rocky History Hiring Dillon Lawson to replace Guerrero feels like a step backward. Lawson was fired mid-season by the New York Yankees in 2023. His time with the Red Sox also ended quickly after just over one year. The Boston team started 10-17 before he was let go. Even Aaron Judge struggled with a career-low bWAR of 4.6 in 2023 while working with Lawson. The Marlins are trading a coach who fixed their offense for one with a poor track record. Trade Talks and Roster Moves While the coaching staff changes, the front office is also eyeing trades. The Seattle Times reported that the Mariners asked about Otto Lopez. A lockout likely begins on Dec. 1, and they are also seeking pitching assistance. The plan is to make offers for pitchers before the work stoppage starts. With pitcher Bradley Blalock released, the Marlins roster now holds 35 players on their 40-man list.

The sought-after Leipzig attacker had a goal or an assist for his club in each of the last five games before the international break. Recent reports suggest Premier League champions Arsenal would go all in for him in January. Nusa's Norway are now level on points with Denmark, who will face Group A4 leaders Portugal later tonight. Fellow RB Leipzig man Willi Orban helped Hungary to a 2-0 victory away at out-of-sorts Georgia. The result put Hungary top of their group in League B before Northern Ireland's game against Ukraine. Köln's defender Luka Lochoshvili and Heidenheim's Budu Zivzivadze featured for Georgia, who are yet to score in the Nations League after five games. A win in Budapest against Northern Ireland would see Hungary promoted back to League A on Tuesday. However, they had to do it without their leader at the backline as the Leipzig center-back is suspended for accumulated yellow cards. item.title: The day Wales thought might never come
item.description: Dafydd Jenkins equalled the world record for number of tackles in a game [Huw Evans Picture Agency] One of the greatest Welsh wins of all time. That is how former Wales captain Sam Warburton described the monumental result against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday. At the time of the kick-off, the All Blacks were effectively the top ranked side in the world following South Africa's loss to France to previous night. So no-one gave Welsh a hope - including Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30/1 during the week. The question, not of when but can, Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset Welsh rugby for 73 years. That wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama. Little wonder then that few wanted to leave the Principality Stadium long after the final whistle had sparked unprecedented scenes of utter joy - and relief - to the strains of Yma O Hyd. That losing run - stretching across 34 matches - has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of Wales players. Warburton was part of the one of the most successful Welsh teams of all time during the Warren Gatland era - but lost all five meetings with New Zealand. item.title: Wales' top-tier survival hopes hit by Norway loss
item.description: Wales' hopes of retaining their top-tier status in the Nations League are hanging in the balance after they were beaten by Norway in Oslo. Craig Bellamy's side shaded a goalless first half in which they created the better chances, but Norway scored with their first shot on target as Antonio Nusa drilled in from the edge of the penalty area after an hour. The World Cup quarter-finalists doubled their lead nine minutes later as Nusa and Manchester City striker Erling Haaland combined for substitute Andreas Schjelderup to tap in. Wales kept themselves in the contest as David Brooks came off the bench to score with a delicate chipped finish, only for Haaland's penalty to wrap up victory for the hosts after Schjelderup was fouled by Connor Roberts. By avenging their defeat in Cardiff a month ago, Norway leapfrog Wales into third place in Group A4, meaning Bellamy's men will finish bottom. Even if they win their final game at home to group leaders and reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday, Wales cannot overtake Norway or Denmark - who are both three points ahead - because of their inferior head-to-head record. As a result, they are almost certain to face a relegation play-off against a League B team in March. Wales analysis: Promising display but no reward David Brooks scored Wales' third goal of their Nations League campaign [Getty Images] Wales earned their first win at this level when they deservedly beat Norway at home a month ago, but despite promising signs in Oslo, they remain without an away victory against a team ranked above them since beating Israel during Euro 2016 qualifying 11 years ago. Bellamy vowed before this encounter that his team would be going "all out" for victory regardless of their opponents' potency; Wales posed the greater threat of the two sides during the first half. Daniel James, Brennan Johnson and Harry Wilson all looked dangerous on the break, with James twice shooting wide after being set up by Wilson, before forcing Norway goalkeeper Egil Selvik into the first save of the game. This was an assured display from Wales, who were also disciplined and alert defensively as they contained their star-studded hosts. That was until the hour mark when their inability to properly clear a Norway corner presented Nusa - the hosts' sharpest player on the night - with the chance to fire in the goal his electric display on the left wing had warranted. Norway's individual star quality was on show as they doubled their advantage and, even with Brooks' deft finish, it was a long way back for Wales. Disappointing as it obviously will be for Bellamy and his players to finish bottom of their group, a probable relegation play-off presents them with a second chance to stay in the top division of the Nations League. What this result also means, however, is that Wales will now not be among the top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying. item.title: Jim Montgomery Backs Dalibor Dvorsky Despite Recent Bench
item.description: John Jones-Imagn Images St. Louis Blues head coach Jim Montgomery is not ready to give up on Dalibor Dvorsky, even after the young forward saw his ice time shrink to just over six minutes in a recent win. The 21-year-old center has hit a rough patch, scoring only four goals and adding one assist through 18 games this season. Yet the coaching staff insists the first-round pick remains a core piece of the roster rather than a candidate for the AHL. Montgomery told reporters that the team still has faith in the player’s future, despite the drop in production and playing time. The numbers tell a stark story for Dvorsky right now. He played just 10:14 in one contest, then saw that number cut to 6:36 during the Blues’ 3-2 victory over the Detroit Red Wings. His move from the center spot on the third line to the wing was a direct attempt to lower the pressure on his game. The Speed Concern Questions about Dvorsky’s skating speed have followed him since before he was drafted 10th overall in 2023. Montgomery addressed these concerns directly after the benching against Detroit, noting that the player must bring more urgency to his shifts. “Just to play faster, play with more conviction. He’s not played to the standard that we want our players to play with and when that happens, you risk the chance of being sat, and that’s what happened,” Montgomery said, as reported by Lou Korac of The Hockey News. It is a tough spot for a young player who started the season scoring in the first two games but has struggled to maintain that pace. Why No Demotion? Despite the slump, the Blues organization has drawn a line in the sand regarding a potential demotion to the minor leagues. The front office and coaching staff do not view sending Dvorsky down as the right move at this stage. Montgomery emphasized the long-term value of the player, stating, “We believe in him.” He explained his reasoning further, saying, “He’s a big part of us … not only because he’s a first-round pick, but he’s a talented young man that we all enjoy coaching, he’s a really good teammate, and it’s just a matter of time.” This public vote of confidence suggests the team is willing to endure short-term struggles to develop a player they see as a long-term asset. The Blues are betting that patience will yield results rather than rushing the process. The Path Forward The coaching staff has made it clear that the standard for playing time is high, and failure to meet it results in sitting on the bench. However, the team has also made it clear that they are not ready to wash their hands of the 2023 draft pick. Dvorsky now faces a critical window to prove he can adapt to the NHL speed and regain the trust of his coaches.

item.description: Mohit Ulva kept his cool when it mattered most. With India needing three runs off the final ball against Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final, the 18-year-old right-hand batter smashed leg-spinner Ahmed Hussain wide of long-off for a boundary to script a stunning one-wicket victory and bring the trophy back to India. Chasing a daunting 338, India were staring at defeat at 252 for eight in the 42nd over. But Ulva and Manal Chauhan turned the contest around with a courageous 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket. item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images This week, the Yankees returned from Las Vegas’s General Managers Meetings. Brian Cashman described the gathering as “an information grab” for the front office. Rebuilding the bullpen sits at the top of his list to fix a roster that won 93 games last season. The team bowed out in the American League Division Series and now seeks to add depth. Fixing the Late-Inning Arms Relief pitching is the main concern after key departures loom. The club issued a qualifying offer to closer David Bednar, valued at $23.15 million. They have also expressed interest in retaining left-hander Tim Hill. Cashman told MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM, according to MLB.com , “It’s our main priority, to be honest.” The current setup faces a major shift since two of the three pitchers going into the eighth and ninth inning are gone. Cashman said, “Two of the three pitchers going into our eighth and ninth inning are gone; Blackburn and Bednar right now are free agents, so we’ve got our work to do. And because of that, I am casting a wide net. We are asking around, and we need to find some stuff so we can feel good and sleep at night.” Adrian Morejon was a prominent trade target in July and could draw interest again in free agency. Offensive Gaps and Payroll Limits The pitching staff includes AL Cy Young Award winner Cam Schlittler, but the offense needs work. Hal Steinbrenner, the managing general partner, cited offensive underperformance as a major factor behind the shortened postseason. At third base, the team seems “open-minded” to pursue an upgrade beyond Ryan McMahon. The Rangers discussed Corey Seager and contacted free agents Luis Arraez, Brandon Lowe, and Carson Kelly. item.description: I guess that’s a tiger. | Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images Name: University of Missouri Location: Columbia, Missouri Whereabouts is that in the state? Not quite precisely dead in the center of Missouri, but it’s close, and it’s about halfway along a drive between Saint Louis and Kansas City. Did I catch that they also claim to be MU, much like our beloved Marquette University? Yes. It’s right there in the top left corner of Missouri.edu — looking into this is how I discovered that the University of Missouri self-identifies as Mizzou for actual collegiate branding reasons, not just athletics — and their Primary Signature Logo has what they call a “stacked MU mark. Shouldn’t they be UM? Sure, but Michigan beat them to that by about 20 years. Okay, so did they beat Marquette to MU? I can’t say for certain when Missouri started using that particular logo, but… Founded: 1839 as the first public university west of the Mississippi River, and thus beating Marquette to existing by 40 years or so. The founding is just when the state legislature passed the bill to create the university, they didn’t actually hold classes until 1841 , but again, that’s still got Marquette’s 1881 beat. Rats. Yeah, it’s a bummer. Hey, I just realized, is this the first time that Marquette has played another MU/UM team for the first four games of a season? If you count Detroit Mercy because they can be called UDM, sure, we can count that as four straight. I honestly can not answer that question without reading the season by season results until my eyes bleed, but I feel pretty confident guessing that it is the first time that’s happened. Shouts to Northern Illinois for breaking up the streak on Wednesday. Enrollment: 28,347 students for the 2026 Fall Semester, with 24,276 as undergraduate students. Nickname: Tigers Why “Tigers”? It dates back to when the school closed in 1862 due to the Civil War and the campus became a Union Army installation. The people of Columbia created a militia to repel Confederate forces that attempted to engage the base, and their tenacity was such that the militia became known as the Fighting Tigers of Columbia. Fast forward to the creating of the football team in 1890, and they proudly took the same nickname. (Photo by Ron Vesely/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | Getty Images As we get closer to an almost certain lockout by Major League Baseball owners, I can’t help but think back to the St. Louis Cardinals team before the strike that ended the 1994 baseball season. Here’s a quick refresher on exactly what led to the work stoppage in MLB in the summer of 1994. On January 18, 1994, the owners approved a new revenue-sharing plan that included a salary cap. One of the arguments back then was that small-market teams would not be competitive unless local broadcast revenue was shared. Also included in the proposal that would eventually be presented to the players was the elimination of salary arbitration and free agency that would begin after four years instead of six. The proposal was officially submitted to the players association on June 14, 1994 and was officially rejected by the MLBPA on July 18, 1994. I bring up this date because I remember being at Busch Stadium just a few days later. I believe it may have been one of the series against the Atlanta Braves in late July 1994. The mood at Busch Stadium in late July of 1994 was tepid and that’s my memory being optimistic. One life memory I have is being at one of the concession stands in old Busch Stadium standing behind a couple of fans talking about how the baseball strike was inevitable and they swore they’d never come back to a game if the players went out on strike. It didn’t help that the 1994 St. Louis Cardinals were not a very good team, either. The St. Louis Cardinals in 1994 had Ray Lankford who was about to enter his prime. He and Todd Zeile had 19 home runs before the season was cut short on August 11, 1994. Ozzie Smith was nearing the end of his playing career. Ozzie was selected to the All-Star game in 1994 at age 39 which made him the oldest player in the game. Gregg Jeffries was arguably one of the best Cardinals players in 1994 with a .325 batting average, 12 home runs and 55 RBI’s. Tom Pagnozzi, Bernard Gilkey, Gerónimo Peña and Mark Whiten were the other regulars in the starting lineup. Brian Jordan was still a year away from making his impact in St. Louis. Bob Tewksbury was the leader of the St. Louis Cardinals pitching staff in 1994 as he notched 12 wins before the season was shortened. Allen Watson, Vicente Palacios, Rick Sutcliffe and Omar Olivares handled the rest of the starting workload. One of the Cardinals biggest issues in 1994 was their bullpen. Mike Pérez started the year as the closer, but struggled with an ERA over 8 before René Arocha took over and saved 11 games before he went down with an elbow injury that required surgery. Williams describes something much more useful: a conversation that can end with him understanding a play better — or with Johnson deciding it shouldn’t be called. The Bears coach wants to expand what his quarterback can handle. He also wants the player executing the plan to believe in it. item.title: Kyrie Irving’s Contract Situation Fuels Trade Rumors Despite Dallas Success
item.description: Credit: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images Cleveland fans face a nightmare scenario on Saturday night as the team prepares to host the Dallas Mavericks. The Cavaliers were stuck in Miami after a nationwide communications issue grounded all flights across the US on Friday. They finally took off at 9 a.m. on Saturday and will land around noon, leaving them just a few hours to rest before tip-off. Donovan Mitchell has publicly asked for the game to be cancelled because of the travel disruption. The team lost to the Miami Heat 133-121 on Friday night before the ground stop kept them from flying home. Now they must play a rested Dallas squad that is sitting above .500 with a 7-5 record. Irving’s Contract Creates Trade Noise While the Cavs deal with travel chaos, the Mavericks are dealing with intense speculation about Kyrie Irving. Declining his $42.4 million player option for next season allows him to become a free agent this summer. This financial situation is the main reason other teams are watching him closely right now. NBA insider Sam Amick wrote that “The lack of a long-term deal between the Mavs and Irving, all by itself, justifies the outside interest.” Even though Irving is playing well, his contract status keeps his name in trade talks. Amick noted that rival teams still rank him first among players who could reshape the playoff race. Irving himself addressed these rumors on Monday to shut down the distraction. He told reporters, according to Yahoo Sports , “I let the team know out of my own mouth that these trade rumors, anything that’s going on with me, do not let this infiltrate our locker room.” He wants the team to focus on what they have built together instead of the noise. Cooper Flagg Carries Dallas Offense The Mavericks are relying on Irving, and 19-year-old Cooper Flagg is having a breakout sophomore season. His per-game average sits just below 25 points, with 50% shooting from the field. Dallas has staked everything on Flagg, who is performing as an All-NBA talent and MVP candidate. Amick noted the Mavericks hold a 7-3 record this season with Irving playing, having lost both games he missed. It is as though Irving never departed following his left ACL tear in early March 2025. Season stats show he averages 21 points while shooting nearly 50/40/90, a rare anomaly achieved by few players. Dallas has a clear advantage on the glass tonight, specifically in offensive rebounding. Cleveland has been outmatched on the boards by most teams this season. Since the two squads rank nearly identical in every major category, the Cavaliers face one of their most even matchups all year. item.title: Tatum And Celtics Survive Raptors Scare To Complete Perfect Road Trip
item.description: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images They erased a 22-point deficit to beat the Toronto Raptors 98-93 on Wednesday night. This gritty victory capped a perfect four-game road trip. Jayson Tatum helped lead the charge, but the whole squad showed they can handle pressure when the game slips away. Many teams would have folded after such a large hole. The Celtics did the opposite. This win was the fifth straight for the team. Clutch Moments From The Bench While Tatum led the offense, the bench players provided the spark needed to close the gap. Derrick White posted a 19-point, 4-block performance that changed the momentum. Neemias Queta sank two free throws with 15 seconds remaining to provide the Celtics a three-point advantage. Teammates expressed strong praise for White after that big defensive stand. Robinson also told Queta to knock down those free throws, highlighting the trust between the players. White responded to the praise with a simple, “I like you.” These exchanges show a team that enjoys playing together. That connection matters more than any single statistic. A Celebration That Went Late The team’s bond was on full display after the final buzzer. The plane heading back to Boston was delayed after the week-long trip, which kept everyone in the locker room longer than usual. The players bantered and played music, with Ron Harper Jr. blasting Olivia Dean on the aux. Payton Pritchard threw out song requests while Robinson asked for some country music. Harper directed the postgame jam sesh despite being among the few players who never entered the ball game. Joe Mazzulla noted the energy from everyone, even those who did not play. “Even the guys that weren’t playing just gave us a lift, energy-wise,” Mazzulla said after the game, according to CelticsBlog . The lift from non-playing guys is rare. It suggests a team that is built for the long haul. Tatum acknowledged the difficult schedule, mentioning they arrived at their Toronto hotel at 3 a.m. “I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t tired today,” he said. Despite the fatigue, the team focused on the big picture. “We talked about the four-game road trip, and we kind of talked about it before the game,” Tatum said. He emphasized that winning these tough games is required for greatness. “If you want to be great, these are games that you have to [win],” he said, according to the Boston Globe . The Celtics did exactly that on Wednesday night.

item.title: Bielema defends Houser following costly turnovers in UCLA loss
item.description: Illinois quarterback Katin Houser struggled against undefeated No. 4 UCLA on Friday night, throwing two costly interceptions as the Fighting Illini fell to the Bruins. Despite the mistakes, head coach Bret Bielema made it clear that his confidence in Houser hasn’t changed. “We’re here because of what he is and who he is,” Bielema said following the loss. Houser and the Illinois offense struggled to find a rhythm throughout the first half, with UCLA’s defensive pressure forcing the quarterback into several difficult situations. Bielema pointed to frustration as a contributing factor in Houser’s first interception. “The first one, I think, was just a frustration throw,” Bielema said. “There were a couple things, a couple hiccups within that series, and he just threw it down the middle of the field there, and their kid capitalized on it.” Things didn’t improve immediately after halftime. Houser threw another interception on Illinois’ opening possession of the third quarter, eliminating an opportunity for the Illini to build momentum. “The one to start the second half, he was trying to avoid a sack,” Bielema said. Despite the turnovers, Bielema emphasized that Houser must continue learning how to handle pressure without putting the football at risk. “Sometimes those moments can’t be created into turnovers,” Bielema said. Houser also took a physical beating throughout the contest, briefly leaving the game late with a bloody nose. “He came out with a bloody nose that was reminiscent of Rocky in any one of his movies,” Bielema said. Still, Bielema praised his quarterback’s toughness and competitive mentality. “He’s a tremendous competitor,” Bielema said. “He gives us a chance every time he’s out there.”

item.title: Who has the most Race to Dubai titles? A list of multiple winners
item.description: Rory McIlroy didn’t eclipse Matt Fitzpatrick at the DP World Tour Championship last year but he did claim the Race to Dubai to move him out of a tie with Seve Ballesteros. McIlroy's seventh season-long title marked his fourth consecutive — and he is now alone in second on the DP World Tour's list, one back of all-time leader Colin Montgomerie. McIlroy could tie Montgomerie on Sunday but he’ll need to overcome points leader Eugenio Chacarra. The Race to Dubai is a points-based standing for DP World Tour members which includes all tour events as well as the four majors championships. It began in 2009, replacing the Order of Merit (money list) as the way to determine a season-long champion. In what was formerly known as the European Tour, Montgomerie won seven straight Order of Merit crowns, from 1993-99. He add an eighth in 2005. McIlroy's first RTD triumph came in 2012. He won back-to-back in 2014-15, and now has four in a row. Ballesteros spread out his six from 1976 to 1991. “I want it, of course I do,” McIlroy said of the Race to Dubai record. “I caught up with Monty this week when he was here a couple days ago. … Look, it seems within touching distance now. I’d love to be the winningest European in terms of Order of Merits and season-long races. “You know, I’ve probably got a few more good years left in me, and hopefully, I can catch him and surpass him.” Here's a list of the most Race to Dubai/Order of Merit victories, dating to the European Tour's beginning in 1972, including all those with multiple wins: 8 — Colin Montgomerie 7 — Rory McIlroy 6 — Seve Ballesteros 3 — Lee Westwood 3 — Sandy Lyle 2 — Bernhard Langer 2 — Nick Faldo 2 — Retief Goosen 2 — Ernie Els 2 — Henrik Stenson DP World Tour Championship 2026: Final-round tee times, pairings and how to watch Here’s how to watch the conclusion to the DP World Tour season, with the Race to Dubai on the line. item.title: Hardaway: Dallas Needs Kyrie To Reach Top Seed
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Tim Hardaway Sr. knows the Dallas Mavericks better than most, and his recent comments cut through the noise. He says the team will not move Kyrie Irving because they need him to win. The Mavericks are 7-2 in games where Irving and Cooper Flagg play together. The Window Is Open Now Early in the season, rumors swirled that Dallas might ship Irving out. Those talks have died down for a good reason. The team sits at 7-5 and has won three of their last four games. Irving missed the entire previous year due to an ACL injury, so his return to form is a massive boost. He is averaging 22.9 points and 4.3 assists while shooting 48.7 percent from the field, per The Smoking Cuban . The offense has jumped from 27th in the league last year to 12th this season. Hardaway believes the Mavericks are aiming for a top spot in the West. Hardaway proclaimed “They gon’ make the playoffs, sure,” during a recent podcast appearance. He went further, stating the team could land as high as the fourth or fifth seed. “They gon’ be in the upper-echelon of the West, they gon’ be like 4 or 5 up there,” Hardaway said. As the No. 8 seed, the team trails the Houston Rockets by only 1.5 games for the No. 3 seed. Why Trading Him Fails An article titled “1 Overreaction To Every NBA Team’s Start” by Zach Buckley on November 12 asserts the Dallas Mavericks’ overreaction is “the Kyrie Irving trade chatter needs to stop.” Buckley noted that the short window with Flagg and Irving should keep speculation alive, yet the on-court results suggest otherwise. Dallas is now the most efficient isolation team in the NBA, ranking first in points per possession and scoring frequency, per The Smoking Cuban. Irving still leads the team in isolation plays, which is crucial for breaking down tough defenses. Even though the Mavericks suffered a bad loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Thursday night, the core duo remains vital.
